ratings_why.fun: Winding the clock so the shop and the fight land on different phases is a real decision every turn, and growth ramps well from turn 3's Full to the Moon-Scour late; the first two turns are thin.
ratings_why.distinct: A visible moon you wind, with Borrow as a doubling layer over other tribes, plays unlike any of today's six tribes, though Borrow-style copying is familiar from other games.

verdict_why: Grandam of the Forms does nothing beyond summoning as written, and Silverpenny's 'biggest' needs a timing; both are small, real fixes.

points.text: Grandam of the Forms fires on New Moon, but Leverets only borrow while the moon is Full, so no Leveret is ever 'borrowing a Hare' then and the copy never happens. Say 'each Leveret with a Hare in front of it' instead.
Sister Silverpenny's 'biggest non-Hare' isn't timed: in a fight the biggest changes as units die and buff. Say when it is checked, e.g. at Start of Combat and at the start of your turn.

The clock build turns the moon three times a shop, so it passes New every turn as well as Full: Silver Sixpence Doe then pays 2 gold a turn (4 with Waxwell) at Tier 2, well above the economy target. Worth the owner's eye, not a cut.
Turns 1 and 2 are vanilla: Moon-Gazer is a 1/2 that only matters once payoffs arrive. A small Moonlit line (e.g. Moonlit: +1/+1) would let it help the turn-3 Full fight too.
Waning is still only Dusk Nurse. One Tier 2 Waning card would make the clock build choose where to stop, not just spin through every phase.

standouts.why: Moon-Caller's mid-fight Full is the surprise that answers 'opponents see your moon', and it makes Waxing a fight phase worth aiming at.
Old Wat is a free moon turn every turn that costs a hand slot: cheap, flavourful, and a real planning piece.
The Moon-Scour gives the late game a shape you chase: every Full you wound earlier pays again.

weakest.why: Moon-Gazer is a weak Tier 1 body whose sell trigger is worth little before Tier 3.
Witch in Borrowed Shape depends on both a Full fight and what the opponent puts across, so its value is mostly luck.

flags.note: As written the Leveret-to-copy step can't happen at New Moon (see p1).
'Biggest' has no timing, so what she borrows mid-fight can't be read.
With Meikle Care and two or three Fulls a shop, the counter climbs 2-3 a turn, so the payout grows roughly quadratically, doubled by Waxwell and spread by The Three Hares.
On a Moonlit fight she kills the enemy across for free and gains +3/+3; with Meikle Care that is every other fight, and a Jack beside her does it too.
In the clock build it pays every turn, 4 gold with Waxwell, from Tier 2.
